1.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
1.subtopic: Magnetic Moment of Current Loop and Galvanometer Instruments
1.solution:
The magnetic moment of the orbiting electron is
\(M = \dfrac{neh}{4\pi m} = n\left(\dfrac{eh}{4\pi m}\right)\).
Hence \(M \propto n\), the principal quantum number.

2.subtopic: Moment of Inertia, Theorems, and Radius of Gyration
2.solution:
For equal mass and radius, \(I_{disc}=\dfrac{MR^2}{2}\) and \(I_{ring}=MR^2\), so \(I_{ring}>I_{disc}\).
With the same torque, \(\alpha=\dfrac{\tau}{I}\propto\dfrac{1}{I}\), so \(\alpha_{disc}>\alpha_{ring}\).
The disc gains angular speed faster, hence it rotates with greater angular frequency.

4.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
4.solution:
In forward bias the applied field opposes the built-in field, so majority carriers cross the junction and the depletion (barrier) region narrows.
Hence the width of the depletion layer decreases.

5.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
5.solution:
Radiated power \(P=\sigma A T^4=\sigma(4\pi R^2)T^4\).
For equal power: \(R_1^2T_1^4=R_2^2T_2^4\Rightarrow\left(\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^2=\left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^4\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{R_2}{R_1}=\left(\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^2\).

6.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
6.subtopic: Force on Moving Charge in Magnetic Field
6.solution:
The Lorentz magnetic force \(\vec{F}=q\vec{V}\times\vec{B}\) is always perpendicular to the velocity \(\vec{V}\).
Since \(\vec{F}\cdot\vec{V}=0\), the work done on the charge is zero.

7.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
7.solution:
Fringe width \(X=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\), so the \(X\) vs \(D\) graph is a straight line through the origin with slope \(\dfrac{X}{D}=\dfrac{\lambda}{d}\).
\(\therefore \lambda=\text{slope}\times d\).

8.solution:
At the centre, fields of \(+q\) (A) and \(+q\) (D) cancel; fields of \(-q\) (F) and \(-q\) (C) cancel.
Field left is that of \(-q\) at B: \(E'=\dfrac{kq}{r^2}\). Field of \(+Q\) at E: \(E=\dfrac{kQ}{r^2}\).
Given \(E'=2E\): \(\dfrac{kq}{r^2}=2\cdot\dfrac{kQ}{r^2}\Rightarrow Q=\dfrac{q}{2}\).

9.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
9.solution:
Two equal inductors in parallel: \(L_T=\dfrac{L}{2}\). Two equal capacitors in series: \(C_T=\dfrac{C}{2}\).
Resonant frequency \(f=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{L_TC_T}}=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{2}\cdot\frac{C}{2}}}=\dfrac{1}{\pi\sqrt{LC}}\).

10.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
10.solution:
Volume conserved: \(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3=64\cdot\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{R}{4}\).
Work \(=\Delta(\text{surface area})\times T=\left[64\cdot4\pi(R/4)^2-4\pi R^2\right]T\).
\(=(16\pi R^2-4\pi R^2)T=12\pi T R^2\).

11.subtopic: Lenses — Lens Formula, Power, and Lensmaker

12.subtopic: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Rolling Motion
12.solution:
For rolling without slipping, \(v=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1+\frac{K^2}{R^2}}}\).
For a solid sphere \(\dfrac{K^2}{R^2}=\dfrac{2}{5}\).
\(\therefore v=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1+\frac{2}{5}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{10gh}{7}}\).

14.solution:
Between P and Q: four capacitors in series \(\left(\dfrac{C}{4}\right)\) are in parallel with one \(C\): \(C_{PQ}=C+\dfrac{C}{4}=\dfrac{5C}{4}\).
Between P and R: a three-in-series branch \(\left(\dfrac{C}{3}\right)\) in parallel with a two-in-series branch \(\left(\dfrac{C}{2}\right)\): \(C_{PR}=\dfrac{C}{3}+\dfrac{C}{2}=\dfrac{5C}{6}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{C_{PR}}{C_{PQ}}=\dfrac{5C/6}{5C/4}=\dfrac{2}{3}=2:3\).

15.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves

16.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
16.solution:
Closed pipe fundamental \(n_1=\dfrac{v}{4L}=150\) Hz.
Open pipe fundamental \(n_1'=\dfrac{v}{2L}=2n_1=300\) Hz, and it produces all harmonics.
Hence frequencies are \(300,600,900,1200,\ldots\) Hz.

17.subtopic: Doppler Effect — Moving Source and Observer

18.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
18.solution:
For the cycle \(\Delta U=0\), so \(\Delta Q=W_{net}=5\) J.
From the graph, \(W_{AB}=P\,\Delta V=10(2-1)=10\) J and \(W_{BC}=0\) (isochoric).
\(W_{net}=W_{AB}+W_{BC}+W_{CA}\Rightarrow 5=10+0+W_{CA}\Rightarrow W_{CA}=-5\) J.

19.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
19.solution:
Second minimum in front of one slit: \(y=\dfrac{d}{2}\), with \(y_n=\dfrac{(2n-1)\lambda D}{2d}\).
For \(n=2\): \(\dfrac{d}{2}=\dfrac{3\lambda D}{2d}\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac{d^2}{3D}\).

21.subtopic: Magnetic Moment of Current Loop and Galvanometer Instruments
21.solution:
Torque \(\tau=IAB\sin\theta\propto A\).
For a given perimeter (same wire length), a circle encloses the maximum area, so the circular loop experiences the greater (maximum) torque.

22.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
22.solution:
By Newton's law of cooling, the heat lost over the same temperature drop equals \((m+x)c\,\Delta T\), and the rate \(\propto\) constant for a fixed mean excess temperature.
Case 1: \(\dfrac{(10+x)}{10}\); Case 2: \(\dfrac{(20+x)}{15}\). Equating: \(\dfrac{10+x}{10}=\dfrac{20+x}{15}\).
\(30+3x=40+2x\Rightarrow x=10\) g.

23.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
23.solution:
Excess pressure in a bubble \(P=\dfrac{4T}{r}\); isothermal coalescence conserves \(PV\):
\(\dfrac{4T}{r_1}\cdot\frac{4}{3}\pi r_1^3+\dfrac{4T}{r_2}\cdot\frac{4}{3}\pi r_2^3=\dfrac{4T}{r}\cdot\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\).
\(r_1^2+r_2^2=r^2\Rightarrow r=\left(r_1^2+r_2^2\right)^{1/2}\).

24.solution:
Balmer series limit \(V_1=\dfrac{RZ^2}{4}\); Paschen series limit \(V_3=\dfrac{RZ^2}{9}\).
First Balmer line \(V_2=RZ^2\left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{9}\right)=V_1-V_3\).
\(\therefore V_1-V_2=V_1-(V_1-V_3)=V_3\), i.e. \(V_1-V_2=V_3\).

25.subtopic: Average KE, Equipartition, and Specific Heats
25.solution:
Cylinder A: heat at constant pressure \(Q=nC_p\,dT_A\). Cylinder B: heat at constant volume \(Q=nC_v\,dT_B\).
Equal heat: \(nC_p\,dT_A=nC_v\,dT_B\Rightarrow dT_B=\dfrac{C_p}{C_v}dT_A=\gamma\,dT_A\).

26.solution:
Output is 1 for inputs (0,0) and (0,1). For OR, (0,0) gives 0; for AND, both give 0; for NOR, (0,1) gives 0. Only NAND gives output 1 for these inputs.
Hence the gate is NAND.

27.solution:
Sum \(\perp\) difference \(\Rightarrow(\vec{A}+\vec{B})\cdot(\vec{A}-\vec{B})=0\).
\(A^2-B^2=0\Rightarrow|\vec{A}|=|\vec{B}|\).
The forces are equal in magnitude.

28.solution:
The bridge is balanced (all \(R=4\,\Omega\)), so the central resistor carries no current.
Paths ACB and ADB each have \(8\,\Omega\); their parallel combination is \(\dfrac{8\times8}{16}=4\,\Omega\).
Total current \(=\dfrac{16}{4}=4\) A, splitting equally: \(I_{ACB}=2\) A.

29.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
29.solution:
In SHM, acceleration \(a=-\omega^2x\); the negative sign means acceleration is antiparallel to displacement.
Hence the phase difference between displacement and acceleration is \(\pi\) rad.

30.subtopic: Self-Inductance, Energy Stored, and LR Circuit
30.solution:
Since \(\phi=LI\), the slope of the \(\phi\)–\(I\) graph equals \(L\).
Line \(L_1\) has the greater slope, so its self-inductance is greater than that of \(L_2\).

31.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
31.solution:
Energy of a wave \(E\propto n^2A^2\). Equal energies: \(n_P^2A_P^2=n_Q^2A_Q^2\).
\(\dfrac{A_Q}{A_P}=\dfrac{n_P}{n_Q}=\dfrac{n}{n/4}=4\Rightarrow A_Q=4A_P\).

32.solution:
Induced emf \(=Blv\), current \(i=\dfrac{Blv}{R}\), retarding force \(=Bil=\dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R}\).
For free fall the magnetic force balances gravity: \(mg=\dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R}\).
\(\therefore v=\dfrac{mgR}{B^2l^2}\).

Mutual inductance \(M=\dfrac{|e_P|}{dI_Q/dt}=\dfrac{12\times10^{-3}}{10}=1.2\times10^{-3}\) H.
Flux in Q when \(I_P=1.5\) A: \(\phi_Q=MI_P=1.2\times10^{-3}\times1.5=1.8\times10^{-3}\) Wb \(=1.8\) mWb.

38.subtopic: Newton's Laws — Force, Tension, Lift, and Connected Blocks
38.solution:
At Q the rope PQ makes angle \(\theta\) with the vertical. Horizontal equilibrium: \(T\sin\theta=F\).
\(\therefore T=\dfrac{F}{\sin\theta}\).

39.solution:
At the mean position momentum is conserved: \(Mv_1=(M+m)v_2\), i.e. \(M\omega_1A_1=(M+m)\omega_2A_2\).
With \(\omega_1=\sqrt{k/M}\), \(\omega_2=\sqrt{k/(M+m)}\):
\(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}=\dfrac{(M+m)\omega_2}{M\omega_1}=\sqrt{\dfrac{M+m}{M}}=\left(\dfrac{M+m}{M}\right)^{1/2}\).

40.solution:
A dielectric reduces the net electric field between the plates, lowering the potential difference for the same charge (thereby increasing capacitance).
Hence its function is to reduce the effective potential on the plates.

41.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
41.solution:
Upward surface-tension force \(F=2\pi rT=(\text{circumference})\times T\).
\(2\pi r=\dfrac{F}{T}=\dfrac{108\times10^{-5}}{7.2\times10^{-2}}=1.5\times10^{-2}\) m \(=1.5\) cm.

42.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
42.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
42.solution:
Stopping potential (left x-intercept) increases with frequency: curves b and c start at the same point \(\Rightarrow f_b=f_c\); curve a starts least negative \(\Rightarrow f_b>f_a\).
Saturation current measures intensity: curves c and d reach the same saturation level \(\Rightarrow I_c=I_d\).
Hence \(f_b>f_a,\ f_b=f_c,\ I_c=I_d\).

43.subtopic: Kinematics — Equations of Motion, Free Fall, and Graphs
43.solution:
Using \(v_f^2-v_i^2=2as\) with \(v_f=0\): \(s=\dfrac{v^2}{2a}\).
For speed \(nv\), same distance: \(s=\dfrac{(nv)^2}{2a'}\). Equating: \(\dfrac{v^2}{2a}=\dfrac{n^2v^2}{2a'}\).
\(\therefore a'=n^2a\).

44.solution:
\(\dfrac{N}{N_0}=\dfrac{2000}{8000}=\dfrac{1}{4}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2\), so 4 min = 2 half-lives \(\Rightarrow T_{1/2}=2\) min.
\(\lambda=\dfrac{\log_e2}{T_{1/2}}=\dfrac{\log_e2}{2}=0.5\log_e2\) per minute.

45.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
45.solution:
First overtone: open \(n_1=\dfrac{v}{L}\), closed \(n_1'=\dfrac{3v}{4L}\). Beats: \(\dfrac{v}{L}-\dfrac{3v}{4L}=\dfrac{v}{4L}=4\Rightarrow\dfrac{v}{L}=16\).
New fundamentals: open (length \(L/2\)) \(=\dfrac{v}{L}\); closed (length \(2L\)) \(=\dfrac{v}{8L}\).
Beats \(=\dfrac{v}{L}-\dfrac{v}{8L}=\dfrac{7}{8}\times16=14\).

46.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
46.solution:
True power \(P=\dfrac{V_{rms}^2}{Z}\cos\phi=\dfrac{V_{rms}^2R}{Z^2}=\dfrac{210^2\times18}{30^2}=\dfrac{44100\times18}{900}=882\) W.
This is nearest to 900 W (\(|882-900|=18\) versus \(|882-800|=82\)).
46.note: Re-derivation gives P = 210^2 x 18 / 30^2 = 882 W. The AK's own worked solution computes 882 W yet keys C (800 W); 882 W is clearly 'nearly' 900 W (option D), not 800 W. Correct answer is D.

47.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
47.solution:
In an isochoric process the volume (not pressure) remains constant; pressure changes with temperature.
Hence the statement 'In an isochoric process, pressure remains constant' is NOT true.

48.solution:
For \(A=\dfrac{pq^2}{r^2s^4}\), \(\dfrac{\Delta A}{A}=\dfrac{\Delta p}{p}+2\dfrac{\Delta q}{q}+2\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}+4\dfrac{\Delta s}{s}\).
\(=3+2(2)+2(3)+4(1)=3+4+6+4=17\%\).

50.solution: Kirchhoff's voltage law (loop rule) is based on conservation of energy; Kirchhoff's current law (junction rule) is based on conservation of charge.

52.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
52.solution:
Benzene-1,2-diol (the ortho-dihydroxybenzene) has the common name catechol.
Resorcinol is the 1,3-isomer; quinol (hydroquinone) is the 1,4-isomer; pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol.

54.subtopic: Preparation Methods of Aldehydes and Ketones
54.solution:
DIBAL-H reduces a nitrile to an imine, which on acid hydrolysis gives an aldehyde (one C from CN becomes CHO).
The C=C double bond is unaffected, so hex-3-enenitrile gives hex-3-enal.

55.solution:
\(ClF_5\) has a square pyramidal shape (6 electron domains, one lone pair).
Among the xenon compounds, \(XeOF_4\) is also square pyramidal (5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair), matching \(ClF_5\).

56.solution:
\(\Delta T_f = K_f \cdot m\).
\(K_f = \dfrac{\Delta T_f}{m} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.18} = 1.11\) K kg mol\(^{-1}\).

57.solution: Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) is naturally obtained from the bark of the willow plant (Salix).

59.solution:
In DNA the sugar is 2-deoxyribose; the \(C_2'\) carbon lacks the -OH group present in ribose (it has only H).
Hence the \(C_2'\) carbon is the one missing oxygen.

60.solution:
For methanal \(CH_2O\): \(x + 2(+1) + (-2) = 0\), so \(x = 0\).
The oxidation number of carbon is zero.

61.solution: Freon-12 is dichlorodifluoromethane, \(CCl_2F_2\), the most common refrigerant.

62.solution:
Sodium acetate (\(CH_3COONa\)) is a salt of a strong base (NaOH) and weak acid (\(CH_3COOH\)); its aqueous solution is basic and turns red litmus blue.
\(CuCl_2\) is acidic; KCl is neutral.
62.note: Options C and D are both printed as 'KCl' (a duplicated option in the source), but this does not affect the unique correct answer A.

63.solution:
Acetic acid + thionyl chloride gives acetyl chloride (A).
Acetyl chloride + ammonia gives acetamide (B), \(CH_3CONH_2\).

64.subtopic: Real Gases, Dalton's Law and KTG
64.solution:
Partial pressure is proportional to moles. Moles: \(H_2 = 5/2 = 2.5\), \(He = 8/4 = 2\), \(CO_2 = 50/44 = 1.14\), \(Ne = 20/20 = 1\).
Ne has the least moles, so it exerts the minimum partial pressure.

65.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
65.solution:
For isothermal reversible work, \(W = -2.303\,nRT \log\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\) (compression).
\(W = 2.303 \times 1 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log 2 = 2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times 0.301\).
\(= 1729\) J \(= 1.729\) kJ.

66.subtopic: Physical Properties of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
66.solution: Boiling point of alcohols increases with molecular mass. Methanol has the lowest molecular mass among the options, so it has the lowest boiling point.

67.subtopic: Unit Cells, Edge Length and Atomic Radius
67.stemOverride: Calculate the radius of an atom of an element in pm if it forms bcc unit cell structure having edge length \(4.3 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm}\).

68.solution:
Aspartic acid (Asp) bears a side-chain carboxyl group and is an acidic amino acid.
Arg and Lys are basic; Met is neutral.

69.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
69.solution:
Lu (Z = 71): [Xe] \(4f^{14}5d^{1}6s^{2}\). On forming \(Lu^{3+}\) it loses the \(6s^2\) and \(5d^1\) electrons, leaving [Xe] \(4f^{14}\).
The 4f subshell is completely filled, so there are 0 unpaired electrons.

70.solution: Electronegativity decreases down a group. Among Li, Na, K, Rb, lithium is at the top, so Li has the highest electronegativity.

71.subtopic: Reactions of Alkenes, Addition, Oxidation and Ozonolysis
71.solution: Alkenes react with cold dilute alkaline \(KMnO_4\) (Baeyer's reagent) to give vicinal diols, i.e. glycols.

72.subtopic: Reaction Mechanism, Intermediates and Rate-Determining Step
72.solution:
The rate law is determined by the slow (rate-determining) step: \(NO_2Cl \rightarrow NO_2 + Cl\).
Applying the law of mass action to this step gives \(r = k[NO_2Cl]\).

73.subtopic: Physical Properties of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
73.solution:
Among isomeric butyl alcohols, boiling point decreases with increasing branching (branching lowers surface area and van der Waals contact).
The straight-chain n-butyl alcohol (butan-1-ol) is the least branched, so it has the highest boiling point.
73.note: Options are structure images of the four isomeric butyl alcohols (n-butyl, isobutyl, sec-butyl, tert-butyl). Option A = straight-chain n-butyl alcohol (butan-1-ol), confirmed from image13. Attach the four option images.

74.subtopic: Molecular Orbital Theory and Bond Order
74.solution:
Bond orders: \(Cl_2\) = 1 (single), \(O_2\) = 2 (double), \(N_2\) = 3 (triple).
Higher bond order means shorter bond length, so decreasing bond length: \(Cl_2 > O_2 > N_2\).

For \(H^+ + e^- \rightarrow \tfrac{1}{2}H_2\) with \(E^{\circ} = 0\), \(P_{H_2} = 1\) atm:
\(E = -\dfrac{0.0592}{1}\log\dfrac{1}{[H^+]} = -0.0592 \times pH\).
With pH = 1, \(E = -0.0592\) V.

77.solution:
A tertiary amine has the nitrogen bonded to three carbon groups and no N-H.
N-Ethyl-N-methylpropan-2-amine has N bonded to ethyl, methyl and isopropyl groups, so it is tertiary.
The others are primary (cyclohexanamine, ethane-1,2-diamine) or secondary (N-phenylbenzeneamine).

78.solution:
Boiling point elevation is proportional to the number of particles (van't Hoff factor i).
\(AlCl_3 \rightarrow Al^{3+} + 3Cl^-\) gives i = 4, the largest of the options (KCl, NaCl: 2; \(BaCl_2\): 3).
Hence \(AlCl_3\) shows the maximum elevation.

79.solution:
Dacron (Terylene) is a polyester made by condensation of ethylene glycol with terephthalic acid.
Option C gives \(HO(CH_2)_2OH\) (ethylene glycol) and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid).

80.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
80.solution:
The +I effect of alkyl groups stabilises the positive charge on the conjugate acid. Stability increases with more alkyl groups: \(NH_4^+ < RNH_3^+ < R_2NH_2^+ < R_3NH^+\).
Hence \(NH_4^+\) (no alkyl groups) is the least stable species.

81.solution: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) is used to determine particle size of nanomaterials.

82.solution:
Friedel-Crafts alkylation of chlorobenzene with chloromethane (anhydrous \(AlCl_3\)) gives ortho and para chlorotoluenes (Cl is an o/p-director).
Hence A is chlorobenzene.

84.solution: Anisole (methoxybenzene) cleaved by HI gives phenol (benzenol) and iodomethane (the aryl-O bond is retained; the alkyl group leaves as the iodide).

85.solution: The statement that orbitals of a subshell are singly filled before pairing is Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity.

88.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
88.solution:
Cell: \(Zn|Zn^{2+}\|Ag^+|Ag\), \(n = 2\), \(E = E^{\circ} - \dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log\dfrac{[Zn^{2+}]}{[Ag^+]^2}\).
Lowering \([Ag^+]\) from 1 M to 0.1 M increases the log term: change \(= -\dfrac{0.0592}{2}\log\dfrac{1}{(0.1)^2} = -\dfrac{0.0592}{2}(2) = -0.0592\) V.
The emf decreases by 0.0592 V.

89.subtopic: Types of Solids, Crystal Systems and Properties
89.solution: The attraction between metal cations and the surrounding sea of mobile (delocalised) electrons constitutes the metallic bond.

90.solution:
In the spectrochemical series, halides are weak-field ligands and \(Br^-\) lies near the weak end: \(I^- < Br^- < Cl^- < ... < NH_3 < CN^- < CO\).
Among \(NH_3\), CN\(^-\), \(Br^-\), CO, the weak field ligand is \(Br^-\).

92.solution: Glycerol slows down (retards) the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide, so it acts as an inhibitor (negative catalyst).

93.subtopic: Preparation of Alkanes, Wurtz, Grignard and Decarboxylation
93.solution:
The Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides with sodium in dry ether to form a biaryl.
Option D, \(2C_6H_5Br + 2Na \rightarrow C_6H_5\text{-}C_6H_5 + 2NaBr\), is the Fittig reaction (biphenyl).
Option A is the Wurtz-Fittig (aryl + alkyl); B and C are Wurtz reactions.

94.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life
94.solution:
For a first-order reaction, plotting \(\log[A]_t\) vs t gives slope \(= -\dfrac{k}{2.303}\).
\(k = -2.303 \times \text{slope} = -2.303 \times (-2.5 \times 10^{-3}) = 5.757 \times 10^{-3}\) s\(^{-1}\).

95.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
95.solution:
A Grignard reagent reacts with dry ice (\(CO_2\)) and then dilute acid to give a carboxylic acid with one more carbon.
\(CH_3CH_2MgBr\) (2 C) gives \(CH_3CH_2COOH\), propanoic acid (3 C).
95.note: Official AK letter is C (2-Methylpropanoic acid) which is wrong. Ethyl Grignard CH3CH2MgBr + CO2 (dry ice) then dil.HCl gives CH3CH2COOH = propanoic acid = B; the AK's own worked solution derives CH3CH2COOH. Correct = B.

96.subtopic: pH, pOH and Ionic Product of Water
96.solution:
For a weak dibasic acid, \([H^+] = \alpha \cdot c \cdot Z\) with Z = 2.
\([H^+] = 0.02 \times 0.01 \times 2 = 4 \times 10^{-4}\) M.
\(pH = -\log(4 \times 10^{-4}) = 3.398\).

97.solution:
\(\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S\). For \(\Delta G < 0\) at all temperatures, need \(\Delta H < 0\) and \(\Delta S > 0\).
Then both terms make \(\Delta G\) negative regardless of T.

98.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
98.solution:
Cu has the higher reduction potential (+0.34 V) than SHE (0.00 V), so Cu\(^{2+}\) is reduced (cathode) and \(H_2\) is oxidised (anode).
Net: \(H_2 + Cu^{2+} \rightarrow 2H^+ + Cu\).

99.subtopic: Complex Types, Homoleptic, Heteroleptic, Cationic, Anionic, Neutral
99.solution:
A neutral complex has no overall charge on the coordination entity.

102.subtopic: Continuity at a Point — Finding Parameters
102.solution:
\(f(x) = \frac{(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)(x+2)}{|x-1||x-2|}\) for \(x \neq 1,2\).
Since \(\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{x-1}{|x-1|}\) and \(\lim_{x\to 2}\frac{x-2}{|x-2|}\) do not exist, \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x=1,2\).
Elsewhere it is a ratio of polynomials, hence continuous on \(\mathbb{R} - \{1,2\}\).

103.solution:
Areas: \(A_1 = x^2,\ A_2 = y^2\).
\(\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = \frac{2y\,dy/dt}{2x\,dx/dt} = \frac{y}{x}\cdot\frac{dy}{dx}\).
With \(y = x - x^2,\ \frac{dy}{dx} = 1-2x\), so \(\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = (1-x)(1-2x) = 2x^2 - 3x + 1\).
